cache/journal.author: A Wayfarer
pages: Autumn. Found the valley today: water, birch, a south slope. The ember brightened at the pond. One winter. I'll build a cabin for one winter.
The cabin stands. I sleep in a bed for the first time since I was a child. The ember is quieter. It's resting, I think. We've walked a long way.
Spring. I meant to go. The roof needed mending, and then the garden. The ember is the size of a pea. It doesn't warm my hand any more.
Second winter. Something scratched at the door last night and went away. It came back the next night. I keep the fire high.
One more winter here. The ember is so small now. I'll walk in spring.
cache/journal.title: A Journal

first_gate/bright_years.author: An archivist of the deep city
pages: We were the brightest city the world had ever seen, and we were proud of it. Our lamps burned day and night. We did not know that every lamp was a word shouted at the sky.
Then the dragon looked. Not at a traveller, not at a village. At us. The light went cold in the streets, and the first of us stopped moving where they stood.
first_gate/bright_years.title: Record of the Bright Years

first_gate/gate_we_built.author: An archivist of the deep city
pages: Our masters found power in the burning world below and built a gate of our own, to strike back through the dark. You have seen its frame at the heart of the city.
It opened once. What came through was silence, and the silence spread across the stone like moss. We call it sculk now. It remembers every sound we ever made.
Do not wake the guard. It is the last of us, and it no longer knows friend from enemy. Walk softly, take what you need, and leave us to the quiet.
first_gate/gate_we_built.title: The Gate We Built

first_gate/last_record.author: An archivist of the deep city
pages: I write this by the gate, because the gate is the only thing in the city still making a sound. It hums, very low, the note it made the day it opened.
What came through was not the dragon's. The dragon only watches. This wants nothing watched, nothing moving, nothing at all. It is patient. It has all the time there is.
If you came down here carrying a light, keep walking. Everything that stops, it finds.
first_gate/last_record.title: The Last Record

gazebound/grass_king.author: The Gazebound
pages: Brothers, the Grass King saw what the dragon sees, and for one summer he ruled as a god. Then his people, cowards all, tore the sight from his crown.
We are his heirs. We will finish what he began: gather the twelve shards, open the true gate, and let the dragon see the world again, through our eyes and for our purposes.
gazebound/grass_king.title: The Crown of the Grass King

gazebound/ledger.author: The Gazebound
pages: Captain Wend, taken in at the grass halls in the first winter. Eats well. Asks for nothing. Walks the halls at night as if they were a road.
Ninth winter: the captain's ember went dark. He hears nothing in it now. We keep him anyway: one day he may give it to someone.
Twentieth winter: the captain is old. The captains agree: let him light his fire by the road, and follow whoever he gives it to.
gazebound/ledger.title: The Captain's Ledger

gazebound/orders.author: The Gazebound
pages: Orders for the captains. The shards are waking and calling to each other. Listen for them in the high places, the dead places, the drowned places.
A Wayfarer is walking again, and gathering for us without knowing it. Do not touch the ember. Let it find what we cannot, and follow its smoke to the gate.
gazebound/orders.title: Orders for the Captains

gazebound/orders_1.author: A Gazebound captain
pages: By the heir's word, to every outpost on the south roads. Watch for smoke where no village stands. A Wayfarer's fire is small, and burns each night in a new place.
Do not fight whoever carries an ember. Do not let them see you follow. Leave them food: a carrier who eats well walks further.
gazebound/orders_1.title: Captain's Orders, I

gazebound/orders_2.author: A Gazebound captain
pages: Our finder's ember has gone dark. It no longer shows him the halls. We keep him at our halls in the grassland anyway: one day he will give his ember to someone.
When the old man lights his last fire by the road and dies there, someone will walk away from it with his ember. Follow that one.
gazebound/orders_2.title: Captain's Orders, II

gazebound/orders_3.author: A Gazebound captain
pages: Never frighten the carrier: a carrier who fears us hides, and walks slower. Let the swamp women and the snow folk think the worst of us. It costs us nothing.
Leave bread where the carrier sleeps. Take nothing from them. Every shard they lift is one we could never lift ourselves.
gazebound/orders_3.title: Captain's Orders, III

gazebound/orders_4.author: A Gazebound captain
pages: To the outposts beyond the sea. The carrier has crossed. Keep to the far shore, and let them find the halls before you do.
Wherever they lift a shard, be there the morning after. Take nothing. Leave nothing but bread.
gazebound/orders_4.title: Captain's Orders, IV

gazebound/orders_5.author: A Gazebound captain
pages: The heir rides to the jungle halls himself. Whatever the carrier cannot open, he will stand beside them and wait.
Keep close to their camp, and closer on the night of the red moon. So it was written in the old captain's own hand, and his page is kept at his house in the dark wood.
gazebound/orders_5.title: Captain's Orders, V

gazebound/shadow_circle.author: The Gazebound
pages: Why do we build our mansions in the dark woods? Because the Shadow Circle built there first. We copied their halls stone by stone, and still their power would not come to us.
They say the burden is the point. They say the shard must be carried, not kept. They are dead, and we are not. Keep searching.
gazebound/shadow_circle.title: The Halls of the Shadow Circle

jungle/prayer.author: The Jungle Folk
pages:
Sleep, little locks. Sleep, and keep what is ours.

Sleep through the rain and the root and the years. Sleep through every hand that is not ours.

Our stone sleeps while you sleep. Let it sleep until our children come home.

Only the word our children knew will rouse you, and our children knew one word before all others: WAKE.
jungle/prayer.title: The Jungle Folk's Prayer

keepers/breaking.author: The Keepers
pages: The Eye sat in the portal between the worlds, and through it the dragon watched everything that stood still. Where it looked, its creatures came. That is how the deep cities fell.
Those who lived tore the Eye out of the portal, and the dragon went blind. They meant to destroy it. Fire, the sea and the hammer could only break it.
Whole, it would sit in any frame again. So they broke it in twelve, and sent each shard to one of twelve peoples at the far ends of the world, to hide.
Its light came loose when it broke. Those who carried it walked, and swore it: never settle, never shine, everything carried. We call them Wayfarers.
Note for the reader. A frame takes whatever of the Eye it is brought. One shard or twelve, it closes the same. Do not let anyone tell you otherwise.
keepers/breaking.title: The Breaking

keepers/distance.author: The Keepers
pages: Why so far? Because the gaze sees what stays still, and a gate stays stiller than anything. We carried this one out past the edge of every map, so that whatever it shone, it shone on nobody.
Twelve halls like this one stand in a ring, all the same distance from where the first fire was lit, and every one of them guards a gate. The ember will lead you to the nearest.
Do not blame us for the walk. Every step between you and home is a step between home and the dragon.
keepers/distance.title: On the Distance of the Gate

keepers/first_watch.author: The Keepers
pages: Year one of the watch. We built this hall as far from everyone as our legs could carry the stone. The gate sleeps below us. It is only a frame now, and we mean to keep it that way.
Rule of the watch: no Keeper lights a fire bigger than a hand. No Keeper plants what takes more than a season to grow. We are the only people in the world allowed to stay, and we must stay small.
If you are reading this, the watch has ended or the Eye is coming home. Either way, you are welcome at our table. There is not much left on it.
keepers/first_watch.title: The First Watch

keepers/last_keeper.author: The Keepers
pages: The last entry. The others have gone down to sleep with the old Keepers. I stay to write, because someone should.

Years ago a Wayfarer came to our door, the only one in my lifetime. His ember was dim, and he wore the grass crown of the Gazebound under his cloak. He asked where the twelve halls lie. No Wayfarer asks that.
We sent him away. If he found someone to carry what he could not, and it is you: do not open this gate for them. Open it for yourself, finish it, and then go home.
keepers/last_keeper.title: The Last Keeper

keepers/wend.author: A Keeper
pages: The finder came to our door again tonight. His ember is the size of a pea. He asked to stay one winter, only one, and said he was tired.
We told him what we tell them all: a Wayfarer who stops lets the gaze in. He said we had shut him out. He cursed us, and the oath, and the road.
He walked off towards the grey coats' fires. Seal this, and pray we were right.
keepers/wend.title: A Keeper's Note

malgven/bundle.author: M.
pages:
Across the sea already. He'd have been proud of you, the old fool.

Eat something warm tonight.

- M.
malgven/bundle.title: A Note

malgven/last.author: M.
pages:
You fly now. I never could keep up with him either.

Eat. He never ate enough either.

- M.
malgven/last.title: The Last Note

malgven/note.author: M.
pages:
For whoever carries his light now.

Eat. It is a long road on an empty stomach.

- M.
malgven/note.title: A Note

malgven/unsent.author: Malgven
pages: Captain Wend. I know you cannot read this. I write it anyway, the way you taught me to talk to the fire.
The one you chose is walking. The captains have me follow the smoke for them. You chose well: they stopped for a dying man when nobody else would. I have not decided what that means.
malgven/unsent.title: A Letter Never Sent

people/black.author: The Tide Folk
pages: We are the Tide Folk, and this is our bay. Nothing comes up out of it at night, so our boats go out with lamps lit, and we eat.
The Drowned City's last swam in on a winter tide with their stone in a net between them, and asked us to keep it from the eye that drowned them. We swore on the fire pit.
If you are reading this, you carry a fire in your hand, and you know what lies on our stone. Take what you must. Leave us the dark.
people/black.title: The Tide Folk

people/cold.author: The Frost Walkers
pages: We are the Frost Walkers. We walk all summer and come home to this hall for the winter, to the stone that remembers.
Tonight someone came down the stair while we slept. When the lamps were lit again, the stone was empty. The young ones ran up after him.
I am too old for the stair. The shouting up there has stopped. I can hear the snow.
One of ours is still out on the hunt. If she comes home, tell her not to wait for us. Tell her to keep walking.
people/cold.title: The Frost Walkers

people/corrupted.author: The Grass Kingdom
pages: The Grass Kingdom was given its shard to hide. Its king kept it instead, on a throne, where everyone could see it.
The shard showed him what the dragon sees, and he wanted more. He was the first of the Gazebound.
His own people tore the shard from his crown and sealed it here. The throne is dust. Do not keep what you carry.
people/corrupted.title: The Grass Kingdom

people/cryptic.author: The Scribes of the Peaks
pages: The Scribes climbed as high as the land would let them and wrote down everything the shard whispered.
Most of it was madness. Some of it was the way the true gate was built, and why it must never be built again.
We burned the madness and kept the rest. The shard we leave to you. Read before you carry it.
people/cryptic.title: The Scribes of the Peaks

people/evil.author: The First Village
pages: The First Village was built by Wayfarers who swore they would only stay one winter.
They stayed a hundred. Their priests said the shard in their temple kept them safe. It was the shard that kept them seen.
When the gaze came, the last priest carried it out into the grass and buried it here. The village is gone. The grass remembers.
people/evil.title: The First Village

people/exotic.author: The Drowned City
pages: We were the Drowned City, the most beautiful place on the coast. Beautiful things are seen. The eye looked at us for one summer, and the sea came up and took the city.
The few of us left climbed up here to our hall in the red rock and lifted our stone's shard, and carried it down to the one bay on the coast the eye could not see.
The Tide Folk keep it now, under their fire pit. If you came here for it, you came to the wrong shore.
people/exotic.title: The Drowned City

people/lost.author: The Diggers
pages: We dug down because the eye in the sky cannot see through stone. The shard hums on its stone in this hall, and while it hums, the ground above us stays dark to that eye.
Our children grew up under lamps and never missed the sun. But the seams near the hall ran out, and the young ones wanted to follow the ore down, past the shard's ground.
We go down with them tonight. If you are reading this, we did not come back up. Take the shard if you must, and walk softly in the deep.
people/lost.title: The Diggers

people/magical.author: The Shadow Circle
pages: The Shadow Circle learned to bend the shard's light into spells. The Illagers learned from them, and learned the wrong lessons.
Their mansions in the dark woods are copies of our halls, built by people who wanted the shard's power without its burden.
The burden is the point. Carry it.
people/magical.title: The Shadow Circle

people/old.author: The Sand Singers
pages: We are the Sand Singers. We dug this hall under the dunes and set our stone in it, and sang to it, and the desert was quiet around us.
One summer the deep sand opened and something came up and swallowed the stone whole. It grew. It sees. Nothing on two legs crosses its ground, so no raider troubles us now.
We sing to it, and it lets us be. If you have come for our stone, it is in the worm. Walk softly.
people/old.title: The Sand Singers

people/rogue.author: The Jungle Folk
pages: We were the Jungle Folk. Our shard taught us how red dust carries a thought from one stone to the next, and we built locks that never slept.
The eye looked for our stone for a hundred summers and never found the way in. So it looked at us instead, one by one, until nobody was left to open the locks.
Our stone sleeps. If you woke it, you knew our word, and you are welcome. We are sorry there is nobody left to say so.
people/rogue.title: The Jungle Folk

people/undead.author: The Grave Keepers
pages: The Grave Keepers buried the Wayfarers who fell on the road, under the oldest trees, where the ground is soft.
They noticed that the dead are never seen by the gaze, and they took the undead shard to hide among them.
We are among them now. Take the shard and keep walking. We will keep the graves.
people/undead.title: The Grave Keepers

people/witch.author: The Marsh Mothers
pages: We brewed with all the swamp gave us, and the shard gave our water its sight. A cup from our pool showed the sick what ailed them, and the lost where they were.
Then the water showed us something looking back. Far off, past every sky, an eye was searching, and the clearer our water saw, the nearer it came.
So we sank the shard in the mud, where no reflection lives, and went down the long stair only when a fever would not break. Our daughters keep the hut over the stair.
If you came by the water, you came the hard way. The stair is ours, and it shows itself to eyes that see true. Leave our daughters their cups.
people/witch.title: The Marsh Mothers

shipwright/log.author: A shipwright
pages: Day 1. Pushed off at dusk on the tide. Edda didn't come down to the water. She'll be on the jetty when I'm back.
Day 3. No land in any direction. Something knocked the hull in the night, twice. A log, I tell myself. Logs don't knock twice.
Day 6. I keep the lamp hooded after dark. Whatever knocks comes when it sees a light.
Day 9. Land. A bay where they fish by night and nothing comes for them. Their boats go out with lamps lit, and the water lies flat as a floor.
Day 11. They gave me water and dried fish, and a name for their bay I can't spell. Turning home tomorrow.
Day 14. Halfway, by the stars. It's back. It follows the lamp, so the lamp's out. It follows anyway. Tell Edda
shipwright/log.title: A Shipwright's Log

tide/remedy.author: Murdo
pages: For the healer of your caravan. Bladderwrack and salt, steeped a night in the water of our bay. Drink it warm.
It breaks the marsh fever. It does one thing more: for a day, the night's creatures look past you. We use it on the boats. Use it well.
tide/remedy.title: The Tide Folk's Remedy

wend/first_camp.author: A young Wayfarer
pages: First night on my own road. I own a tent, a mallet and a fire, and I have never been this happy. Tomorrow I walk until the ember gutters, then I turn.
Whoever finds this: the road gives more than it takes. Eat what it gives, keep your fire small, and never stay where they are kind to you for long.
wend/first_camp.title: A Young Man's Page

wend/last_camp.author: An old Wayfarer
pages: I stopped walking here. My feet hurt and the road was long, and the men in grass cloaks were kind.
They left bread by my fire. I ate it. Tomorrow I will walk on. I wrote that yesterday too.
wend/last_camp.title: The Last Page

wend/ledger.author: Wend
pages: The swamp's hall, under the black pool. The snow hall, the stair, twenty winters gone. The old green, empty. The bay: two, and they bow. The red canyons, empty.
The sands: in the worm. The jungle: locked, and the boy has the maps now. The grasslands: under the seal. The dark wood: here, on my own stand.
The girl. Malgven. Mine now.
wend/ledger.title: His Ledger

wend/letter.author: Wend
pages: For Malgven. Open it at the gate.
Watch the smoke, Malgven. Someone kind is carrying my ember to the gate. Help them finish it, then go and build a home.
wend/letter.title: For Malgven

wend/orders.author: Wend
pages: To the heir. Do not chase the one who carries it. Feed them, and let them walk. The ember pulls them to the halls, and a carrier who eats well walks further.
Let the peoples think the worst of us. If they fear us, they send the carrier on quickly. If they trust us, they keep the carrier talking.
When the last shard is lifted, wait at the frame. They will open it, because they will think it is theirs to open. I will not be there. Find someone to carry it.
wend/orders.title: Orders, in His Hand
